IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r1.claim: These readers pronounce شقوتنا with kasra on shīn and without alif; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use fatḥa and alif.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم ﴿ شقوتنا ﴾ بكسر الشين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r2.speaker: أبان عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r2.claim: A report from Abān says ʿĀṣim allowed either reading of شقوتنا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r2.anchor: قالا حدثنا بشر بن هلال قال حدثنا بكار عن أبان قال سألت عاصما فقال إن شئت فاقرأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r4.claim: Their “misery overcame us” means it took and mastered them; misery ordinarily means an evil outcome, but al-Jubbāʾī says it means desire and indulgence because these cause misery, while another view calls it what was decreed and foreknown.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r4.anchor: وقيل: الشقوة الهوى وقضاء اللذات لأن ذلك يؤدي إلى الشقوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r5.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r5.claim: Several authorities read “shaqāwatunā” with alif in the pattern of saʿāda; Qatāda and al-Ḥasan also have a kasra variant, while the majority use the common Hijazi form with a still qāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r5.anchor: والمفضل عن عاصم وأبان والزعفراني وابن مقسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r6.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites Abū Tharwān's verse as poetic evidence for the hardship reading of “shaqāwatunā.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: أنشدني أبو ثروان وكان فصيحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r1.speaker: شبل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r1.claim: Shibl reads “shaqwatunā” with fatḥa on the shīn and a still qāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r1.anchor: وقرأ شبل في اختياره بفتح الشين وسكون القاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r2.claim: “We were a misguided people” means they had strayed from guidance; their confession leads into a plea for release from Hell, promising not to return to disbelief and idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p586/r2.anchor: وكنا قوما ضالين أي عن الهدى، ثم تدرجوا من الإقرار إلى الرغبة والتضرع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read شقاوتنا with alif and fatḥa; both forms are dialectal, and they blame a written destiny for their misguidance.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r5.claim: They confess that their misfortune mastered them and led to a bad end; Hamza and al-Kisa'i read shaqāwatun with fatḥ, and another reading has kasr.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r5.anchor: ملكتنا بحيث صارت أحوالنا مؤدية إلى سوء العاقبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r5.claim: The majority read shaqwatuna with kasra and no extra alif; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read shaqawatuna with fatḥa and an alif, while Asim permits both.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «شقوتنا» بكسر الشين دون ألف بعد القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r6.claim: After admitting guilt, they move to pleading; confession is an apology and disavowal, but God's decreed reply is to drive them away and silence them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r6.anchor: ثم تدرجوا من الإقرار إلى الرغبة والتضرع وذلك أنهم ذلوا لأن الإقرار بالذنب اعتذار

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r10.claim: Shaqawa is the opposite of happiness and harm that reaches someone in the outcome.
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r10.anchor: والشقاوة: ضد السعادة، وهو المضرة اللاحقة في العاقبة

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r11.claim: Ghalaba is prevailing by force; kuluh is grimacing, opposite to a pleasant face.
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r11.anchor: والغلبة: الاستعلاء بالقوة. والكلوح: مصدر كلح، وهو خلاف الطلاقة

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.anchor: will desire to go back to the world in order to do good instead of evil, though it will be too late for them (vv.99–118)

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r6.claim: Wretchedness is the opposite of happiness; a person's allotted good is lost in wretchedness, or wretchedness is the evil that characterizes them.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r6.anchor: وعادة الشيء ما يختص به من الخير

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r7.claim: Their wording that misery overcame them hints that they acquired it through bad choices; their promise to act well if returned confirms that their state relates to voluntary action.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r7.anchor: وفي إضافة الشقوة إلى أنفسهم تلويح إلى أن لهم صنعا في شقوتهم من جهة اكتسابهم ذلك بسوء اختيارهم

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r8.claim: They imagine themselves as neutral beings overcome by misery, but their misery is their own through bad choices and deeds; this is an admission that the proof against them was complete.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r8.anchor: الشقوة شقوة أنفسهم أي شقوة لازمة لسوء اختيارهم

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r9.claim: Their confession and denial on Judgment Day merely express settled dispositions: some lie and deny the truth despite seeing it.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r9.anchor: كما أنهم يكذبون يومئذ وينكرون أشياء مع ظهور الحق ومعاينته لاستقرار ملكة الكذب والإنكار في نفوسهم

TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq explains that their own deeds made them wretched.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r5.anchor: عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } قال بأعمالهم

TABRISI:23:101/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101/r1.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:23:101/r1.claim: Both readings, shiqwatuna and shaqawatuna, are sound; the former is a verbal noun like raqqah and fitnah, while the latter parallels saʿādah.
TABRISI:23:101/r1.anchor: الشقوة مصدر كالرقة والفطنة والشقاوة كالسعادة فالقراءة بهما جميعا سائغة

TABRISI:23:101-108/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r14.claim: Their shiqwah is the harm that overtakes well-being; the evil deeds that caused their misery overcame them, and neglecting God for idols and desire is the gravest misery.
TABRISI:23:101-108/r14.anchor: استعلت علينا سيئاتنا التي أوجبت لنا الشقاء

THALABI:v7p57/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r9.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
THALABI:v7p57/r9.claim: They read شقاوتنا with an alif and a fatḥa on shīn, while other readers use شقوتنا without alif and with kasra; both are dialect forms.
THALABI:v7p57/r9.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم: شقاوتنا بالألف وفتح الشين، غيرهم: شقوتنا بغير ألف وكسر الشين

THALABI:v7p57/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p57/r10.claim: شقاوة is harm that comes in the end, while سعاده is benefit that comes in the end.
THALABI:v7p57/r10.anchor: وهي المضرة اللاحقة في العاقبة، والسعادة هي المنفعة اللاحقة في العاقبة

THALABI:v7p57/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p57/r11.claim: The people confess that they had strayed from guidance and ask to leave the Fire.
THALABI:v7p57/r11.anchor: ربنا أخرجنا منها أي من النار فإن عدنا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r2.claim: The passage first gives God's response to the damned, then their confession and plea for release.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r2.anchor: The first of these verses expresses the response of God when these people would wail and cry. Thereafter their confession and request are cited.

SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r1.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read shaqāwatanā with fatḥa on shīn and a long ā after qāf; others have shaqwatanā with kasra on shīn and vowelless qāf.
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان: " شقاوتنا " بفتح الشين وألف بعد القاف

SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r2.claim: The forms are verbal nouns with the same meaning; shaqāwa resembles qasāwa and is widespread, while shaqwa resembles fiṭna and niʿma and is Hijazi.
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r2.anchor: وهما مصدران بمعنى واحد، فالشقاوة كالقساوة

SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line with shaqwatihi as evidence for the Hijazi form.

SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r4.speaker: قتادة والحسن
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r4.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan in one transmission match the two readers' long-vowel form but use kasra on shīn.
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r4.anchor: قرأ قتادة والحسن في رواية كالأخوين إلا أنهما

SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r5.speaker: شبل
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r5.claim: Shibl's preferred reading matches the majority's short form but has fatḥa on shīn.
SAMIN-DURR:23:106/r5.anchor: وشبل في اختياره كالباقين، إلا أنه فتح الشين

ASAD-NOTES:23:106/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:106/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:106/r1.claim: The condemned blame their misfortune for leading them astray and beg to leave their suffering, promising to be counted among evildoers if they sin again.
ASAD-NOTES:23:106/r1.anchor: O our Sustainer! Our bad luck has overwhelmed us, and so we went astray![62]

ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r1.claim: In this context shiqwah means abstract bad luck, the sinners’ futile excuse for their own failings.
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r1.anchor: abstract "bad luck" (which is the meaning of shiqwah in this context)

ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r2.claim: The allegorical dialogue exposes a common excuse and indirectly stresses free will and responsibility for human actions and behavior.
ASAD-NOTES:23:106#n62/r2.anchor: stresses the element of free will - and, therefore, of responsibility - in man's actions and behaviour.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read shaqāwatunā with fatḥa and an alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (شقاوتنا) بفتح الشين وبالألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r2.claim: The other readers use shiqatunā with kasra and no alif; Asim permits either form in a report quoted by the author.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: شقوتنا بكسر الشين بغير ألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r3.claim: Both forms are acceptable: shaqwa is a verbal noun like ridda and fiṭna, while shaqāwa is like saʿāda.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p302/r3.anchor: الشقوة: مصدر كالردة، والفطنة، والشقاوة: كالسعادة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r1.claim: The word is read with kasra on shīn and no alif, or fatḥa with alif; both are verbal nouns or nouns derived from misery.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بكسر الشين من غير ألف وبفتح الشين وإثبات الألف وكلاهما مصدران أو اسمان مشتقان من الشقاء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r2.claim: Shiqāwa follows the pattern of salāma, while shiqwa follows the pattern of fidya.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p258#2/r2.anchor: فأما الشقاوة فكقولهم سلم سلامة وأما الشقوة فكقولهم فديته فدية

NASHR:v2p329/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p329/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p329/r6.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read شقوتنا with fatḥa on both consonants and an alif; the rest use kasra on shīn, sukūn on qāf, and no alif.
NASHR:v2p329/r6.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بفتح الشين والقاف وألف بعدها، وقرأ الباقون بكسر الشين

QIRAAT-ER:23:106:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:106:5#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:106:5#1/r1.claim: The alternative masdar shaqāwa is a common faʿāla pattern, while shiqwa is the rarer fiʿla; both derive from sh-q-w.
QIRAAT-ER:23:106:5#1/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: Alternative masdar form shaqāwa vs shiqwa — both are valid verbal nouns of sh-q-w

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r1.claim: Their wretchedness overcame and mastered them; attributing it to themselves signals that it arose from their own bad disposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r1.anchor: أي استولت علينا وملكتنا شقاوتنا التي اقتضاها سوء استعدادنا كما يوميء إلى ذلك إضافتها إلى أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r2.speaker: شبل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r2.claim: Shibl reads شقوتنا with fatḥa on the initial shīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ شبل في اختياره شقوتنا بفتح الشين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وحمزة والكسائي والمفضل عن عاصم وأبان والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r3.claim: These readers have شقاوتنا with fatḥa on shīn and an alif after qāf.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله واتلحسن وقتادة وحمزة والكسائي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r4.speaker: قتادة والحسن عن خالد بن حوشب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r4.claim: Qatada, and al-Hasan in Khalid ibn Hawshab's transmission, read شقاوتنا with alif and kasra on shīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ قتادة أيضا والحسن في رواية خالد بن حوشب عنه ( شقاوتنا ) بالألف وكسر الشين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r5.claim: All forms are verbal nouns meaning the opposite of felicity; a group glosses them as the evil end God knew their deeds deserved, a view attributed to most Mu'tazilites.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r5.anchor: وهي في جميع ذلك مصدر ومعناها ضد السعادة وفسرها جماعة بسوء العاقبة التي علم الله تعالى أنهم يستحقونها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r6.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r6.claim: The Ashʿarites interpret their wretchedness as the disbelief and sins God had written for them in eternity.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r6.anchor: وعن الأشاعرة أن المراد بها ما كتبه الله تعالى عليهم في الأزل من الكفر والمعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r7.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r7.claim: Al-Jubba'i understands wretchedness metaphorically as desire and pursuit of pleasures, naming the cause by its effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r7.anchor: المراد بها الهوى وقضاء اللذات مجازا من باب إطلاق المسبب على السبب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r8.claim: Rather than personification as a settled agent, the wording is best treated as a representational metaphor: an affair originating in themselves prevailed over them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r8.anchor: فنسبة الغلب إليها لاعتبار تشبيهها بمن يتحقق منه ذلك ففي الكلام استعارة مكنية تخييلية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r9.claim: On every account of wretchedness, their words confess that God's proof stood against them: its source was their own condition, so they cannot claim injustice in punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r9.anchor: ومرادهم بذلك على جميع الأقوال في الشقوة الإعتراف بقيام حجة الله تعالى عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r10.claim: They were astray from truth and denied the recited signs; their words acknowledge that God does not wrong them in punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r10.anchor: عن الحق مكذبين بما يتلى من الآيات فما تنسب إلى حيف في تعذيبنا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r11.claim: Al-Alusi rejects an excuse based on God's foreknowledge or decree: God wrote only what He knew, and knowledge follows what is known, including their poor disposition and resulting choices.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p67#2/r11.anchor: فإنه سبحانه ما كتب إلا ما علم وما هم عليه في نفس الأمر من سوء الاستعداد المؤدي إلى سوء الاختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r5.claim: They say their wretchedness overcame them, meaning their desires led them into evil deeds that became the apparent cause of misery.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r5.anchor: أهواؤنا التي قادتنا إلى سوء الأعمال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p223/r6.claim: They were a people astray from guidance and steeped in causes of misery, as if captive to them and driven by devils.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r1.claim: Mujahid explains their misery as the misery that had been written for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : غلبت علينا شقوتنا التي كتبت عليهم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains “astray” as ignorant.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2508/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : ضالين يقول : جاهلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r5.claim: غلب is literally to overpower; here it means being overtaken by misery rather than happiness, with the object ‘happiness’ understood from the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r5.anchor: والغلب حقيقته : الاستيلاء والقهر . وأطلق هنا على التلبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r6.claim: The object of غلبت is omitted but supplied by شقوتنا: their misery overcame happiness; the following على phrase names what was overcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r6.anchor: لأن الشقوة تقابلها السعادة ، أي غلبت شقوتنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r7.claim: The preposition على after a form of ‘overcome’ marks what is overcome, as in the hadith phrase ‘the men have prevailed over us.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r7.anchor: والمجرور ب ( على ) بعد مادة الغلب هو الشيء المتغالب عليه كما في الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r8.claim: Their freely choosing causes of misery over causes of happiness is pictured as a state of inner contest in which misery gained the upper hand; it became theirs as it dominated them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r8.anchor: مثلت حالة اختيارهم لأسباب الشقوة بدل أسباب السعادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r9.claim: The majority read شقوتنا with kasra on the shīn and a still qāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r9.anchor: والشقوة بكسر الشين وسكون القاف في قراءة الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r10.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read شقاوتنا with fatḥa on the shīn and an alif after the qāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف { شقاوتنا } بفتح الشين وبألف بعد القاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r11.claim: Adding قوما depicts misguidance as a defining trait and part of their collective identity, as in other Qur’anic descriptions of peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127#2/r11.anchor: وزيادة قوله { قوما } على أن الضلالة من شيمتهم

BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r2.claim: They say their misery, acquired through their bad choices, mastered them and led their circumstances to an evil end.
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r2.anchor: التي اقترفناها بسوء اختيارنا فصارت أحوالنا مؤدية إلى سوء العاقبة

BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r3.speaker: القرطبي
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the best explanation that their pleasures and desires overcame them; they are called misery because they lead to misery.
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r3.anchor: القرطبي : وأحسن ما قيل في معناه غلبت علينا لذاتنا

BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r4.speaker: أبو تراب
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r4.claim: Abu Turab defines misery as thinking well of oneself and thinking badly of other people.
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r4.anchor: أبو تراب : الشقوة حسن الظن بالنفس وسوء الظن بالخلق

BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r5.claim: They were astray from the truth, which explains their denial and their other sins.
BURSEVI:v6p77#3/r5.anchor: ولذلك فعلنا ما فعلنا من التكذيب وسائر المعاصي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r1.claim: These readers pronounce shaqwatunā with kasra on shīn and no alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر شقوتنا بكسر الشين من غير الف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r2.speaker: عمرو بن العاص وأبو رزين وأبو رجاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r2.claim: These readers pronounce shaqwatunā with fatḥa on shīn and no alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عمرو ابن العاص وابو رزين العقبلي كما ورد في المصدر و الأصح العقيلي وأبو رجاء العطاردي كذلك إلا أنه بفتح الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r3.claim: These readers pronounce shaqāwatunā with an alif and fatḥa on shīn and qāf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r3.anchor: والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي شقاوتنا بألف مع فتح الشين والقاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada also read with an alif and fatḥa on qāf, but kasra on shīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة كذلك إلا أن الشين مكسورة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r5.claim: The commentators say the people admit that the misery decreed for them kept them from guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p492#2/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون أقر القوم بأن ما كتب عليهم من الشقاء منعهم الهدى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r3.claim: They admit the proof was established, but their wretchedness kept them from submitting and following it; they strayed and were not granted guidance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p498/r3.anchor: أي: قد قامت علينا الحجة، ولكن كنا أشقى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r1.claim: Ghalabat ʿalaynā means it mastered and possessed them, as when someone takes something from another and owns it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r1.anchor: {غلبت علينا } ملكتنا ، من قولك : غلبني فلان على كذا ، إذا أخذه منك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r2.claim: Their wretchedness is the evil end God knew they deserved because of their evil deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r2.anchor: والشقاوة سوء العاقبة التي علم الله أنهم يستحقونها بسوء أعمالهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r3.claim: The word is read shaqwatunā or shaqāwatunā, with either fatḥa or kasra on the shīn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r3.anchor: قرىء : { شقوتنا } وشقاوتنا بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they make six appeals, each for a thousand years, answered by refusal or rebuke; the cited sequence includes 32:12, 40:11–12, 43:77, 14:44, 35:37, and 23:99,108.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p207/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : إن لهم ست دعوات : إذا دخلوا النار قالوا : ألف سنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.claim: One explanation takes their misery as their own desires or passions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.anchor: قوله : { قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : الهوى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is their good opinion of themselves and bad opinion of other people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : حسن الظن بالنفس وسوء الظن بالخلق .

MUJAHID:v2p434#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p434#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p434#3/r1.claim: Their misery is the fate that had been written for them.
MUJAHID:v2p434#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ غلبت علينا شقوتنا ﴾ يعني التي كتبت عليهم

MUQATIL:23:106-111/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:106-111/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:106-111/r1.claim: Their wretchedness overcame them because it had been written for them.
MUQATIL:23:106-111/r1.anchor: قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } التى كتبت علينا { وكنا قوما ضآلين

MUQATIL:23:106-111/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:106-111/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:106-111/r2.anchor: وكنا قوما ضآلين } [آية: 106] عن الهدى، ثم قالوا:

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r2.claim: Hamza and Ali read shaqwatunā; other readers read shaqāwatunā. Both are verbal nouns for misery.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r2.anchor: ﴿ شقوتنا ﴾ شقاوتنا حمزة وعلى وكلاهما مصدر أى شقينا بأعمالنا السيئة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r3.claim: He rejects the exegetes’ claim that a prewritten decree of misery overwhelmed them: God writes what a person does and knows he will choose, so the person is neither overpowered nor compelled.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r3.anchor: وقول أهل التأويل غلب علينا ما كتب علينا من الشقاوة لا يصح لأنه إنما يكتب ما يفعل العبد وما يعلم أنه يختاره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r4.claim: They call their own sinful deeds the cause of their misery; this is an excuse for their neglect, not grounds for absolution.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r4.anchor: وهذا لأنهم إنما يقولون ذلك القول اعتذارا لما كان منهم من التفريط فى أمره فلا يجمل أن يطلبوا لأنفسهم عذرا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#6/r5.claim: They were astray from the truth and what is right.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم والكوفيون وابن مسعود والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r1.claim: Medinan readers, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAsim read shaqwatuna; the Kufans except ʿAsim read shaqawatuna, also reported from Ibn Masʿud and al-Hasan.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r1.anchor: أبي عمرو وعاصم «شقوتنا» وقرأ الكوفيون إلا عاصما «شقاوتنا»

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r2.claim: The words shaqāʾ and shaqā are also used, respectively with a long or short vowel.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r3.claim: The best explanation is that their pleasures and desires overcame them; they are called misery because they lead to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r3.anchor: وأحسن ما قيل في معناه: غلبت علينا لذاتنا وأهواؤنا فسمى اللذات والأهواء شقوة، لأنهما يؤديان إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r4.claim: The Qur’an similarly names the punishment that follows an act by the consequence already contained in it: consuming orphans’ wealth unjustly is described as eating fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r4.anchor: كما قال الله عز وجل: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r5.claim: Another view says their misery was what God had foreknown and written for them in the Mother of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r5.anchor: وقيل: ما سبق في علمك، وكتب علينا في أم الكتاب من الشقاوة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r6.claim: A further explanation is that they thought well of themselves and badly of other people.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r6.anchor: وقيل: حسن الظن بالنفس وسوء الظن بالخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r7.claim: They confess that their actions had led them away from guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r7.anchor: أي كنا في فعلنا ضالين عن الهدى

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r8.claim: This is a confession, not an excuse; their subsequent plea to leave Hell and promise not to return to wrongdoing supports that reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r8.anchor: وليس هذا اعتذار منهم إنما هو إقرار. ويدل على ذلك قولهم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAmr reports that Hell’s inhabitants call Malik for forty years without reply; he eventually answers that they will remain there.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r9.anchor: عن قتادة يذكره عن أبي أيوب عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r10.claim: In Ibn ʿAmr’s report, they then call on God, are left unanswered for twice the span of the world, and are told to be driven away; afterward they speak no words, making only the sounds of donkeys—first an exhalation, then an inhalation.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r11.claim: Al-Tirmidhi also transmits a similar account as a Prophetic report from Abu al-Dardaʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r11.anchor: خرجه الترمذي مرفوعا بمعناه من حديث أبي الدرداء

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r12.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r12.claim: Qatada compares the disbelievers’ voices in Hell to a donkey’s bray, beginning with an exhalation and ending with an inhalation.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: صوت الكفار في النار كصوت الحمار، أوله زفير وآخره شهيق

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the people of Hell will make barking sounds like dogs.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يصير لهم نباح كنباح الكلاب

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r14.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r14.claim: Muhammad b. Kaʿb al-Qurazi begins a report he says he heard about the people of Hell crying to the keepers; al-Qurtubi notes the full account in his al-Tadhkira.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107/r14.anchor: محمد بن كعب القرظي: بلغني أو ذكر لي أن أهل النار استغاثوا بالخزنة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r1.claim: In Muhammad b. Kaʿb’s account, after God reminds them that they had denied His signs, they expect mercy and repeat their plea; they interpret their “misery” as the decree written for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r1.anchor: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r2.claim: The report says God tells them to be driven away and speak no more; their supplication and hope cease, they bark at one another, and Hell is shut over them.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:106-107#2/r2.anchor: فانقطع عند ذلك الدعاء والرجاء، وأقبل بعضهم على بعض ينبح بعضهم في وجوه بعض، وأطبقت عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses “our wretchedness overcame us” as “our settled character overcame us,” like someone taking something from another.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : غلبت علينا ملكتنا

RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains shaqāwa as an evil final outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r3.anchor: قرىء : ( شقوتنا ) و ( شقاوتنا ) بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r4.claim: Both shaqwatunā and shaqāwatunā are reported, with the initial consonant read with fatḥa or kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r4.anchor: قرىء : ( شقوتنا ) و ( شقاوتنا ) بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r5.claim: Abū Muslim relates shaqwa to shaqāʾ, like jarya to flowing: the form can name a state, so here it means the condition of misery.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108/r5.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الشقوة من الشقاء كجرية الماء

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r1.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r1.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says pursuit of forbidden pleasures and eagerness to do evil led to misery; they name the cause by its effect while admitting culpability, not offering an excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r1.anchor: قال الجبائي : المراد أن طلبنا اللذات المحرمة

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r2.claim: If choice arose without a cause, preference without cause would undermine proof of a Creator; if caused, its origin must be examined.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r2.anchor: فإن حصل باختيارهم فذلك الاختيار محدث

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r3.claim: If a servant’s choice needs a determining cause, another preference-maker entails regress; uncaused preference between possibilities is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r3.anchor: فإن توقف صدور تلك الإرادة عنها إلى مرجح آخر

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r4.claim: A servant does not know the quantity or manner of actions and so cannot originate them; otherwise precise ordering would not establish divine knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r4.anchor: العبد لا يعلم كمية تلك الأفعال ولا كيفيتها

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r5.claim: People seek knowledge rather than ignorance; since even unbelievers intend knowledge but may become ignorant, God creates motives toward good or evil, producing felicity or wretchedness.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r5.anchor: فالكافر ما قصد إلا تحصيل العلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r6.claim: If their alleged deviation were identical to denial, denial would explain itself circularly; deviation must be an antecedent cause, a created motive toward error.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r6.anchor: إن كان هو نفس ذلك التكذيب لزم تعليل الشيء بنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r7.claim: God’s command to be driven away and not speak affirms that disputation with God is impermissible and He is not questioned about His acts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r7.anchor: وهذا هو صريح قولنا في أن المناظرة مع الله تعالى غير جائزة

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī says they had no excuse beyond confession; if they knew God created and willed their unbelief, they would more naturally cite it as an excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r8.anchor: قال القاضي في قوله : { ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } دلالة

RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r9.claim: Rāzī replies that their statement already gives that causal account, but they admit it does not excuse them; therefore God tells them to be silent.
RAZI-FULL:v23p108#2/r9.anchor: ولكنهم مقرون أن لا عذر لهم

STUDYQURAN:23:105/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r1.speaker: R and Z
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r1.claim: The verb rendered “overwhelmed” can mean taking possession, ownership, or dominion over something.
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r1.anchor: The verb phrase rendered overwhelmed has the sense of taking possession or ownership of or dominion over something (R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:23:105/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r2.claim: The disbelievers’ statement is read as describing God’s role in making them wretched, because He decreed their wretchedness in the Mother of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r2.anchor: they are describing God’s role in making them wretched, meaning that God destined in the Mother of the Book that they should be so (43:4; Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:105/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r3.claim: On this interpretation, their words are treated as a statement of fact, not a plea.
STUDYQURAN:23:105/r3.anchor: In this sense, it is not understood as a plea, but as a statement of fact (Q).

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the rebuke as Qur'anic verses recited and rejected in worldly life, then the sinners answer in the Hell scene by saying decreed wretchedness overcame them.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r1.anchor: قال ابن جريج: بلغنا " أن أهل النار نادوا خزنة جهنم: أن {ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب} [غافر: 49]

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r2.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r2.claim: Most readers of Medina and Basra and some Kufans read shiqwatunā with kasra on shīn and without alif.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r2.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة: {غلبت علينا شقوتنا} [المؤمنون: 106] بكسر الشين، وبغير ألف.

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r3.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r3.claim: Most Kufan readers instead read shaqāwatunā with fatḥa on shīn and an alif.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r3.anchor: وقرأته عامة قراء أهل الكوفة: «شقاوتنا» بفتح الشين، والألف.

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī judges both readings famous and equivalent in meaning, and says a reader is correct with either one.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان، وقرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القراء بمعنى واحد، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب.

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r5.claim: They say the misfortune decreed for them in God's prior knowledge and inscribed in the Mother of the Book overcame them.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r5.anchor: قالوا: ربنا غلب علينا ما سبق لنا في سابق علمك، وخط لنا في أم الكتاب.

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r6.claim: Mujāhid explains their misfortune as what had been written for them.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {غلبت علينا شقوتنا} [المؤمنون: 106] قال: «التي كتبت علينا»

TAB-FULL:v17p116/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r7.claim: In a report Ibn Jurayj says the people of Hell successively petition its keepers, Malik, and God; after delays and refusals, God tells them to be cast away and remain silent.
TAB-FULL:v17p116/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: بلغنا " أن أهل النار نادوا خزنة جهنم: أن {ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب} [غافر: 49]

TAB-FULL:v17p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p118/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p118/r1.claim: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that Hell's inhabitants call to Paradise's inhabitants; the latter answer with God's curse and deny them water or provision because it is forbidden to disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v17p118/r1.anchor: قال: ثني حجاج، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، قال: " ينادي أهل النار أهل الجنة فلا يجيبونهم ما شاء الله،

TAB-FULL:v17p120/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb recounts the condemned's repeated pleas: Malik delays and confirms their stay; they try patience, seek death or return, repent, then cite their written misfortune; God silences them and only howling remains.
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r1.anchor: قال: سمعت محمد بن كعب، زاد أحدهما على صاحبه قال محمد بن كعب: " بلغني أو ذكر لي، أن أهل النار استغاثوا بالخزنة،

TAB-FULL:v17p120/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r2.speaker: الأزهر بن أبي الأزهر
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r2.claim: Al-Azhar ibn Abī al-Azhar, as cited by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, connects the final silencing of Hell's inhabitants with the verse saying that on that Day they will not speak or be allowed to make excuses.
TAB-FULL:v17p120/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن المبارك في حديثه: فحدثني الأزهر بن أبي الأزهر أنه قال: فذلك قوله: {هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون} [المرسلات: 35]

TAB-FULL:v17p121/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r1.claim: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh swears that afterward the people of Hell speak no words, only gasping and wailing forever without end.
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r1.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، أنه قال: «فوالذي أنزل القرآن على محمد، والتوراة على موسى، والإنجيل على عيسى، ما تكلم أهل النار كلمة بعدها

TAB-FULL:v17p121/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam tells Abū Jaʿfar al-Qāriʾ that the people of Hell do not breathe.
TAB-FULL:v17p121/r2.anchor: قال: أخبرني زيد بن أسلم «أن أهل النار لا يتنفسون»

SULAMI:v2p39#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p39#3/r1.speaker: أبو تراب
SULAMI:v2p39#3/r1.claim: Abu Turab identifies wretchedness with thinking well of oneself and holding a bad opinion.
SULAMI:v2p39#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو تراب : الشقوة حسن الظن بالنفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r1.claim: Another reading is شقاوتنا; the forms are synonymous verbal nouns, patterned like سعادة and ردة / فطنة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says their misery overwhelmed them in worldly life, so they were not guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: غلبت علينا شقاوتنا في الدنيا فلم نهتد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r3.speaker: القرظي، مجاهد، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r3.claim: Al-Quraẓī, Mujāhid, and Muqātil say the misery that overwhelmed them was decreed for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p73#2/r3.anchor: وقال القرظي (¬7)، ومجاهد (¬8)، ومقاتل (¬9): غلبت علينا شقاوتنا التي كتبت علينا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r2.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r2.claim: Ibn Mujahid, quoting his father, says their misery was what had been written for them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r2.anchor: تفسير ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: التي كتبت علينا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r3.claim: They admit that they were a people gone astray.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says a wretched person is wretched in the womb, while a happy person learns from another's fate.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r4.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال: سمعت عبد الله بن مسعود يقول: الشقي من شقي في بطن أمه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r5.claim: Yahya notes that the Prophet's report that a person's wretchedness or happiness is written in the womb was discussed elsewhere.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p417/r5.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الحديث عن النبي عليه السلام أنه يكتب في بطن أمه شقيا أو سعيدا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.claim: At the afterlife judgment, God reminds the disbelievers that they denied His recited revelations; this sin is singled out because their other evils began with that rejection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r1.anchor: Allah inkârcılara, âyetleri kendilerine okunduğunda onları yalanlayıp reddettiklerini hatırlatır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r2.claim: Their reply truthfully admits that their evil inclinations dominated them and that they became a misguided people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r2.anchor: Kötü yanımızın etkisinde kaldık; biz bir sapkınlar topluluğu olduk

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r3.claim: Their denial and rebellion arose from failing to overcome appetites, self-interest, and human weakness, not from sincere inquiry or reasoned conclusions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r3.anchor: inkâr ve isyanları samimi araştırmalarına, akıl ve düşüncelerinin vardığı fikirlere değil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.claim: Their plea to be brought out will go unanswered because they should have made it during worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r4.anchor: “Bizi buradan çıkar!” feryatları da karşılıksız kalacaktır. Çünkü bu yakarışları dünyada yapmaları gerekirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.claim: In worldly life, sincere Muslims prayed and prepared for salvation while disbelievers mocked them; now the believers have attained the happy outcome.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:105/r5.anchor: o inkârcılar bu günahsız müminleri küçümseyip alaya alıyorlardı. Ama şimdi mutlu âkıbeti o müminler elde etmişlerdir

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r4.claim: They say that the wretchedness decreed for them overcame them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r4.anchor: غلبت علينا شقوتنا } التي قضيت علينا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r5.anchor: وكنا قوما ضالين } أقروا على أنفسهم بالضلال

ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r4.claim: The word is also read شقاوتنا, with no change in meaning.

ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r5.claim: They acknowledge that they were a people astray.

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r4.claim: Mujahid says the misery that overcame them was the misery decreed for them.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا} قال: شقوتهم التي كتبت عليهم

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r5.claim: Al-Hasan read the word as shaqāwatunā, using the alternative form for misery.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r5.anchor: عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ (غلبت علينا شقاوتنا)

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r6.speaker: إسحق
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r6.claim: Ishaq reports that Abdullah's reading has shaqāwatunā.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r6.anchor: عن إسحق قال: في قراءة عبد الله (شقاوتنا)

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r7.claim: The Prophet describes the damned seeking food, drink and relief: choking fare and scalding water lead them to plead with keepers, Malik and God, until God orders them silenced and they despair.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يلقى على أهل النار الجوع حتى يعدل ما هم فيه
